explanations: The cursor carries both created_at and id, and the ORDER BY uses (created_at DESC, id DESC), but the continuation filter only compares created_at (`AND created_at < ?`). The id half of the cursor is never used. When several tickets share the same created_at (bulk imports, email batches, coarse timestamps) and a page boundary falls between them, every remaining ticket with that exact timestamp is excluded from the next page and is silently never returned. The filter should be a row comparison such as (created_at, id) < (?, ?).

The extra row is only used for `hasMore = rows.size() > pageSize`; it is trimmed off by subList and never returned. Nothing re-includes the cursor row, nothing is cached, and deletions are not compensated for.

New tickets sort to the front (created_at DESC), so with OFFSET every insert would push earlier rows down and cause duplicates on the next page. The cursor anchors on a position in the ordering instead. The ORDER BY is still required, no total count is computed, and random page access is not possible with an opaque cursor.

decode runs at the top of listOpenTickets, before a connection is acquired. A Base64 failure is an IllegalArgumentException, a missing ':' gives StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, and NumberFormatException is a subclass of IllegalArgumentException; all are converted to InvalidCursorException and mapped to 400 by the @ExceptionHandler. The cursor is not silently ignored and the database is never reached.
